title: Federal Officers Shoot Man in The Bronx, NYPD Says
why: Federal officers shot a man in the Bronx, according to the NYPD, adding to a string of shootings involving immigration-enforcement agents. Who fired and under what authority will decide whether New York City police and prosecutors can investigate federal agents on their own turf.

title: How America's Patchwork of Death-in-Custody Rules Is Failing Families
why: Rules on what jails and prisons must tell families after a death in custody differ so much from state to state that many relatives cannot get basic answers about how their loved one died. The reporting gives legislators elsewhere a concrete gap to close.

title: Anti-trafficking activist Tim Ballard says LDS Church 'excommunicated' him to hide child abuse in the faith
why: Tim Ballard, the anti-trafficking activist, alleges the LDS Church expelled him to silence his claims about child abuse inside the faith. The accusation lands on one of Utah's most powerful institutions and will be tested by how the church answers.

title: San Diego politicians blast DOJ voter-record subpoenas
why: The Justice Department has subpoenaed voter records, and San Diego officials are objecting weeks before the Nov. 3 election. How counties respond could set a template for other jurisdictions that receive similar demands.

title: Federal judge rejects the Oakland Diocese's bankruptcy plan
why: A federal judge rejected the Oakland Diocese's bankruptcy reorganization plan, a setback for the diocese's effort to resolve its liabilities through Chapter 11. The ruling affects survivors waiting on any settlement and other dioceses using the same strategy.

title: Colorado counties will reconfigure voting systems to count only eligible passenger rail votes
why: About 800,000 Colorado voters received a passenger rail ballot question they cannot vote on, and counties must now reprogram their systems to count only eligible votes. The fix will determine whether the measure's result holds up with ballots already going out.

title: Albany's Top Lobbying Firm Starts Its Own Super PAC
why: Albany's top lobbying firm has formed its own super PAC, putting the money that influences legislators and the clients who pay it in the same operation. The structure invites scrutiny of campaign-finance rules written without it in mind.

title: Police face barrage of questions but provide few answers about shooting by Williston officer
why: Williston police faced a barrage of questions about an officer's shooting and gave few answers at a public briefing. The thin disclosure so soon after the shooting is a test of Vermont's transparency norms on police use of force.

title: Lamont faces criticism over 'cozy' relationship with Eversource
why: Critics say Gov. Ned Lamont is too close to Eversource's CEO while ratepayers face rising bills. The issue bears directly on how the utility is regulated heading into the election.

title: Pentagon: Execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed
why: The Pentagon says the execution of the Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed, a rare step for a military execution. The decision sets a precedent for public access to federal executions.
